description: What counts as a `[[wikilink]]`, stated twice in TypeScript: the scanner the rename rewriter mirrors (WIKILINK_RE / findWikilinks, itself a registered note-rules-ts-rust copy) and the micromark tokenizer the Milkdown editor parses with. They exist separately because a regex over raw text cannot be a micromark text construct; a disagreement is a data bug — the editor shows a chip the rewriter will not rewrite (a rename silently breaks the link), or the rewriter rewrites text the editor showed as prose. Why the tokenizer is hand-written rather than an adopted library: docs/plan/milkdown-transition.md §3.8 (the #101 survey).
note: LOCKED: syntax.test.ts asks both implementations the same corpus — 34 hand-picked inline edges plus a 10×8 target×frame cross-product — through a REAL Milkdown editor, and fails on any divergence. Two deliberate differences are asserted separately: wikilinks inside code spans and fences (the editor is right there per docs/spec/editor.md, and the raw-text scanner has no notion of code), and a `\|` inside a GFM table cell, which the editor reads as `|` the way mdast-util-gfm-table reads it in inline code (no rename outcome differs: `|` is a forbidden title character, so such a target never resolves).
